newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends down but off the day's lows.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends down but off the day's lows.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended weaker but commission house buying late lifted the market off the day's lows, traders said.
"It looks like mostly commission house buying in here," a trader said. "Benson Quinn bought two million December and that was the big play on the buy side."

Wheat had opened firmer on surprisingly high USDA export data. USDA reported 737,000 tonnes exported in the week ended Oct. 10 -- more than double the previous week's tally and 75 percent above the four-week average. Still, traders noted U.S. wheat prices remained high relative world values. "The U.S. is still not competitive on the world market," a trader said.
Wheat tumbled to the day's lows at midsession as a move below $4.28-1/2 in the December triggered sell stops.
Slow farmer selling lent support but traders noted ideal winter wheat seeding conditions and cited forecasts for a hard freeze in western Nebraska and northwest Kansas this weekend.
"We're expecting some very good freezes in the western hard red winter wheat belt," the trader said. "This is going to perhaps help wheat to go into dormancy."
Wheat ended 1/2 to five cents per bushel lower with December down 2-1/2 at $4.30 a bushel.
Hard red winter wheat volume was estimated at 31,135 contracts, the Kansas City Board of Trade said.
